newsitem.title: UK: BT, Viag start proceedings against Global One. [CORRECTED 17:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: BT, Viag start proceedings against Global One. [CORRECTED 17:40 GMT]

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc said it and its German partner Viag had launched legal proceedings in Germany against Global One to prevent it from breaching European competition rules.

Global One, which was created to provide worldwide telecom services to corporate customers, is a joint venture between Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom and Sprint Corp from the U.S. (Corrects to add France Telecom.)
A BT spokesman said the proceedings were aimed at preventing Global One from carrying out its businesses as long as some EU conditions were not met.

It added that Global One was only given EU clearance on condition that its competitors can obtain supplies from two operators in addition to Deutsche Telekom and France Telecom. (Corrects to France Telecom, from Sprint.)
But licences for such operators have yet to be granted in France and Germany, BT said.
A BT spokesman told Reuters the legal proceedings were also aimed at speeding up the issue of sufficient licences by the relevant authorities.
Three licences were awarded in Germany on Tuesday, but two of these were purely local ones, while only one was an international licence. At least one other international licence was needed, he said.

The legal proceedings come nearly a week after industry sources said that Viag Intercom, the joint venture between Viag and British Telecom, and five other firms filed a complaint in Brussels over the licence issue.

In their Brussels complaint, the six firms said that, while Deutsche Telekom will grant big discounts to its customers, it is charging rivals inflated prices for leased-lines, preventing them from offering competitive prices.
The licence row comes just weeks before Deutsche Telekom's international share listing.

British Telecom, meanwhile, said it and Viag Interkom expect the necessary licences will be granted in the near future, adding this "...is essential for the attainment of fair and effective competition in Europe."
